stories.title: Documented public API
stories.question: Does the product have an API, documented on a public page, that an agent can use to read and change the core records?
stories.full: Public API documentation that covers the product's core records: reading and changing them, or, for a data product, querying its data.
stories.partial: The vendor says it has an API but shows no public documentation, or the documentation is behind a login, partner program or request; or the API covers only a small part of the product, or only reads records a customer would need to change.

stories.title: Official MCP server
stories.question: Does the vendor publish an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for the product?
stories.full: The vendor documents an MCP server it maintains, with setup steps.
stories.partial: The vendor says it has an MCP server but shows no setup steps, or the server is in beta, preview or waitlist, or it covers only a small part of the product.

stories.title: Official CLI or SDK
stories.question: Does the vendor publish an official command-line tool or software development kit?
stories.full: A vendor-maintained SDK or CLI on a public package registry or in a public repository.
stories.partial: Only code samples, an unofficial library the vendor points to, or an SDK available only to partners.

stories.title: Webhooks or events
stories.question: Can an agent subscribe to events, such as webhooks, instead of polling for changes?
stories.full: Documented webhooks or event subscriptions for the core records.
stories.partial: Events only through a third-party automation platform, or for a narrow set of events.
stories.na: The source is a published data set with no records that change on a customer's behalf.

stories.title: Scoped credentials
stories.question: Can an agent get its own credentials, limited to what it needs?
stories.full: API keys or OAuth clients with documented scopes, roles or permissions that limit what a credential can do.
stories.partial: Keys or tokens exist, but every credential carries the whole account's access, or scoping is not documented.
stories.na: The API needs no credentials at all.

stories.title: Machine-readable API spec
stories.question: Is there a machine-readable description of the API, such as an OpenAPI or GraphQL schema, that an agent can load?
stories.full: A public, downloadable OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL or similar specification.
stories.partial: A specification exists but only after login, covers part of the API, or is shown in the docs without a downloadable file.

stories.title: Docs written for agents
stories.question: Is the documentation published in a form meant for agents, such as an llms.txt file or Markdown pages?
stories.full: An llms.txt file for the documentation, or Markdown versions of the documentation pages.
stories.partial: An llms.txt file that covers only marketing pages, or Markdown available on only some documentation pages.

stories.title: Sandbox or test environment
stories.question: Can an agent work against a sandbox or test environment before touching live records?
stories.full: A self-serve sandbox, test mode or developer environment, documented for developers.
stories.partial: A sandbox available only on request or to partners.
stories.na: The API only reads published data, so there is nothing to protect by testing first.

stories.title: Bulk export in open formats
stories.question: Can the customer get its records or licensed data out in bulk, in open formats, without the vendor's help?
stories.full: Documented self-serve bulk export or download in CSV, JSON, Excel or another open format.
stories.partial: Export is mentioned without documentation, covers only some records, needs a support request, or uses a proprietary format.

stories.title: Self-serve access
stories.question: Can a sponsor sign up and start using the product without a sales call?
stories.full: Self-serve sign-up for a paid plan or a free trial, with no call required.
stories.partial: Self-serve only for a limited tier or trial, with the main product behind a demo or sales call.

stories.title: Public pricing
stories.question: Are the prices a small sponsor would pay published?
stories.full: Prices or fees for the plans a small sponsor would buy are on a public page.
stories.partial: Only a starting price ("from $X"), or prices for some plans but not the one a small sponsor would buy, or a calculator that shows prices after asking for contact details. A request-a-quote form alone is none.
